entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Talorgan II, also known as Dub Tholargg mac Uurguist, reigned as a king of the Picts in the late 8th century CE, specifically over the Pictish territories south of the Mounth, a significant mountain range in Scotland. His brief but documented rule, primarily attested through the Annals of Ulster, places him within a tumultuous period of Pictish history marked by ongoing power struggles and the consolidation of various Pictish polities. While his lineage is debated, he is often presumed to be a son of the powerful Óengus mac Fergusa, a prominent figure who had significantly expanded Pictish influence, suggesting Talorgan's reign represented a continuation, albeit contested, of a dynastic line.

His tenure as king, concluding with his death in 782 CE, appears to have been largely confined to the southern Pictish regions, distinguishing him from a potential concurrent ruler of the northern Picts. The Annals of Ulster's precise geographical qualifier, 'king of the Picts on this side of the Mounth,' highlights the fragmented political landscape of Pictland during this era. While specific achievements or military campaigns are not detailed for Talorgan II in surviving records, his very existence as a recognized monarch underscores the persistent efforts of various dynastic factions to assert and maintain control over distinct Pictish territories following the death of Óengus mac Fergusa in 761 CE.
